cards.explanation: The answer is False. David asks if he should go up to one of the towns of Judah, and the LORD answers, “Go up.” It's a short, clear yes. No waiting, no guessing, and David gets to ask his next question.
The answer is Hebron. David asks, “Where should I go?” and the LORD replies, “To Hebron.” David asks a clear question and gets a clear answer. I wish my recipe cards were that direct, friends.

The answer is his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. The text says David went to Hebron “…with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.” David asks the LORD where to go, and then he doesn't go alone.

The answer is that they anoint him king over the house of Judah. The text says, “…there they anointed David king over the house of Judah.” The men of Judah come to Hebron and make it official. That's the big moment here, friends.
The answer is Jabesh-gilead. The men of Judah tell David, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.” That's a heavy piece of news. After it, the text says David sent messengers to those men.

The answer is that the LORD bless them for their kindness to Saul. David tells them, “The LORD bless you, because you showed this kindness to Saul your lord when you buried him.” He sends a blessing to the men who buried Saul. He calls it kindness, and I think that's a nice way to say thanks.

The answer is True. David says, “…I will also show you the same favor because you have done this.” He asks the LORD to show them loving devotion and faithfulness, and he adds a promise of his own. A kind word and a promise to match, and I'd bake a whole batch for that.

The answer is strong and courageous. David says, “…be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me as their king.” He tells the men of Jabesh-gilead that Saul is dead. Strong and courageous, friends, that's his message.

The answer is Saul's son Ish-bosheth. Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, takes Saul's son Ish-bosheth and moves him to Mahanaim. Saul's side has a plan of its own. Abner is the one making the move.
The answer is Israel. Abner makes Ish-bosheth king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim and Benjamin, “…over all Israel.” That's quite a list of places. I can barely get my sprinkle jars in order.

The answer is False. Verse 10 says, “The house of Judah, however, followed David.” Ish-bosheth is king over Israel, but Judah follows David. Two kings, two groups, and I'd say that's a lot for one kitchen counter.

The answer is seven years and six months. The text says David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah “…seven years and six months.” Ish-bosheth reigns two years, so David's time in Hebron is longer. That's a good bit of counting, friends.
